subject: Eigenvalue of non-symmetric matrix in Rstan

messages.author: 49fc09081a1a1bc7
messages.subject: Eigenvalue of non-symmetric matrix in Rstan
parts:
Dear all

I am trying to get the eigenvalue for a non-symmetric matrix. In R, we can use the eigen() function. However, I can only find a similar function in Rstan for only symmetric matrix call eigenvales_sym(). Any suggestions how I can get that eigenvalue in Rstan?


Thanks in advance

Jessica

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Eigenvalue of non-symmetric matrix in Rstan
parts:
On Friday, May 6, 2016 at 12:19:52 AM UTC-4, Jessica Wong wrote:
I am trying to get the eigenvalue for a non-symmetric matrix. In R, we can use the eigen() function. However, I can only find a similar function in Rstan for only symmetric matrix call eigenvales_sym(). Any suggestions how I can get that eigenvalue in Rstan?

In the non-symmetric case, you can't guarantee the eigenvalue is real and Stan doesn't do complex numbers.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Eigenvalue of non-symmetric matrix in Rstan
parts:
Can’t you just construct A^{T}A (or A^{T} A) directly, take the eigendecompositon
of that, and take the square-root of any positive eigenvectors directly?

The problem with anything else is that we need to compute gradients in Stan,
so we can’t just introduce arbitrary numerical algorithms that may not have
clean gradients.  If this eigenvalue will appear only as data, then you can
compute it externally and pass it into the Stan program.

Dear Michael

Thank you for your suggestion. I am trying to estimate the transmission parameter of the SIR model using Stan, then use that to estimate basic reproductive number, which is the maximum eigenvalue of the next generating matrix (A). So the eigenvalue does not appear as data. 

I tried your suggestion but found out that eigenvalue of A^{T}A is not the same that of A when A is nonsymmetric. Here is my code:

A <- matrix(c(-149,-50,-154,537,180,546,-27,-9,-25), nrow=3, ncol=3, byrow=T)

A2 <- A%*%t(A)

eigen(A)$value # 3 2 1

sqrt(eigen(A2)$value) # 8.177597e+02 2.474974e+00 2.964524e-03


I have tried other reading in the past few days but still couldn't come up with a better solution in order to get the eigenvalue of a asymmetric matrix in Stan. Please do you have other idea?


Regards

Jessica

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Eigenvalue of non-symmetric matrix in Rstan
parts:
On Tuesday, May 10, 2016 at 5:58:00 AM UTC-4, Jessica Wong wrote:
I have tried other reading in the past few days but still couldn't come up with a better solution in order to get the eigenvalue of a asymmetric matrix in Stan. Please do you have other idea?

If you only need the largest eigenvalue of a nonsymmetric matrix A, you could accomplish that with a while loop, some tolerance to decide when to exit the while loop, and power iteration

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_iteration

This may require a large amount of RAM and still not be particularly effective.

Ben

local linearlization of the SIR model is a reasonable proxy for BRN

SIR models that define BRN from the SIR parameters themselves,
which then makes it easy to compute BRN in the generated quantities
block.
